messages.content: What are the protein sequences encoded by the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes in Homo sapiens and Pan troglodytes (chimpanzee)?

function.name: get_protein_sequence
function.description: Retrieve the protein sequence encoded by a human gene. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

species.description: The species for which the gene is to be analyzed.

message.reasoning: The user wants the protein sequences encoded by BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes in Homo sapiens and Pan troglodytes. We have a tool get_protein_sequence that can retrieve the protein sequence encoded by a human gene. It accepts gene and species optional. The default species is Homo sapiens. So we can call get_protein_sequence for each gene/species pair. The user wants sequences for both species for each gene. So we need to call get_protein_sequence twice: once for BRCA1 in Homo sapiens, once for BRCA1 in Pan troglodytes. Then similarly for BRCA2. The tool returns any type; presumably it returns the protein sequence string. We'll call the tool for each gene/species pair. The user didn't specify any other constraints. So we will call the tool four times. The tool returns the sequence. We'll then provide the sequences. The user might want them in FASTA format or just plain text. The question: "What are the protein sequences encoded by the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes in Homo sapiens and Pan troglodytes (chimpanzee)?" So we should provide the sequences. We'll ask the tool for each gene/species. We'll do four calls.
